trajectory_messages.content:
I've run into a formatter idempotence bug with switch statements that have trailing comments on case clauses.

*   When formatting a JavaScript switch statement, trailing line comments on case clause lines must remain on the same line as their respective case keyword — they must not be moved into a subsequent block statement.

*   When multiple fall-through case clauses each have trailing line comments and the last such clause is followed by a block statement, all trailing comments must be preserved on their original case lines in the formatted output.

*   The formatter must be idempotent for this pattern: formatting the already-formatted output of such a switch statement a second time must produce exactly the same result as the first format pass.

*   This correct comment placement must apply in both 2-space and tab indentation modes.


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

## Summary

I fixed a formatter idempotence bug in Biome's JavaScript formatter (`crates/biome_js_formatter/src/comments.rs`) where trailing line comments on `case` clauses with a hugging block body were incorrectly moved into the block on a second format pass.

### Root cause

When a `case` clause's body is a single block statement, the opening brace hugs the `case` line (`case foo: {`). A trailing line comment written *before* the brace attaches (by default) as a trailing comment of the case's test expression and prints as a line suffix on the `case` line:

```js
case foo: { // comment
```

But on the **second** pass, that comment now sits right after the `{` — its enclosing node is the `JsBlockStatement`, with no preceding node and the first statement as the following node. The default placement then made it a *leading* comment of the first statement, moving it onto its own line inside the block:

```js
case foo: {
	// comment
```

This broke idempotence. (Note: `default:` clauses already had a dedicated handler with different — but self-consistent — behavior; `case` clauses had none.)

### The fix

Added `handle_switch_case_clause_block_comment`, registered in the `EndOfLine` placement chain. When a line comment directly follows the `{` (no preceding node) of a block that is the single hugging body of a `JsCaseClause`, it re-attaches the comment as a trailing comment of the case's test expression — exactly where the first pass places it — so both passes produce identical output.

The handler is narrowly scoped:
- Only line comments (block comments untouched).
- Only when the comment has no preceding node (own-line comments deeper in the block are unaffected).
- Only when the block is the single hugging block body (`is_single_block_statement_consequent`, mirroring the `JsCaseClause` formatter's own check), so non-hugging separate blocks and `default` clauses keep their existing behavior.

### Verification

- Idempotent across all tested scenarios in **both tab and 2-space** modes: single/multiple fall-through cases, comment before vs. after the brace, complex test expressions (`case foo.bar:`, `case baz():`), and mixed brace-line + own-line comments.
- No regressions: **273** spec tests and **1464** Prettier-compat tests pass.

Per instructions, I only modified source (`comments.rs`) — no test files were touched.
